conviction_note: No company-level number the market has not seen: the print turns on the Q3 FY27 cc guide (consensus -2% to 0%), peers (ACN +19% on 2026-10-01, TCS +5.5% on 2026-10-09, HCL cc +2.3% q/q) lifted the sector and WIT +7.2% in 5 days, and Wipro has sold off on its guide on 3 of its last 4 prints, against a crowded ADR short (14.2 days to cover) that cushions a negative; findings net to 0.0 and p_up 47 on abs 4.0 gives -0.24, the small gap being the guide-sell-off habit weighed slightly more than the squeeze.
bar: Q2 FY27 IT services revenue guide $2,574-2,627m, -1.5% to +0.5% q/q cc (Wipro Q1 FY27 release, 2026-07-16, https://www.itiger.com/hans/news/2651420824); brokerage poll -0.5% to -1.0% cc q/q incl. ~0.7pt Mindsprint, IT services EBIT margin +40bp to ~16.4%, Q3 guide expected -2% to 0% cc (Emkay, Nuvama) or organic -1.5% to +0.5% (Jefferies) (https://www.kotakneo.com/news/stocks/wipro-q2-fy27-results-preview/ 2026-10-14; https://www.tradingview.com/news/moodys:ab25a0f6a0c64:0-wipro-q2-preview-brokerages-expect-weak-revenue-growth-margin-recovery/). MOFSL models Q2 IT services $2,587m (-1.0% q/q USD) (https://investmentguruindia.com/editorial/uploads/news-pdf/1f35dc01_WIPRO-20260716-MOFSL-RU-PG012.pdf). Bar is sourced to the company guide plus several agreeing brokers.
positioning_check: ADR short interest 102,750,718 sh at 2026-09-30 settlement, 14.18 days to cover, up from 62,960,626 (11.86 DTC) on 2026-08-14 and 103,622,630 on 2026-09-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/wit/short-interest, read 2026-10-14). That is ~1% of Wipro's ~10.5bn shares but crowded relative to ADR turnover. No usable option chain (ATM legs not two-sided), so no skew; put/call open interest 3.42 on 615 contracts total (thin). Tape: +7.19% 5d, +6.55% 20d, -41.5% from 52w high, 11% off 52w low.

findings.finding: Peers who reported after Wipro last spoke printed better than feared: TCS Q2 FY27 cc +0.5% q/q with BFSI +2.5% cc (stock +5.46%), HCLTech cc +2.3% q/q with FY27 guide 2.5-4% retained and services EBIT 18.2%, and Accenture beat its own Q4 guide and guided FY27 +3-6% LC (stock ~+19% on 2026-10-01); MOFSL had expected BFSI to recover for Wipro in Q2, so a Wipro cc print at the top half of -0.5% to -1% consensus is more likely than the bottom.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 (2026-07-16): revenue miss vs Rs24,776cr LSEG est, Indian shares +1.77%, ADR -0.28% to $1.83; reported-quarter lines have not been what moved this name, the guide has (https://www.indiainfoline.com/news/companies/wipro-q1-fy27-results-profit-rises-marginally-margins-fall-to-15-quarter-low-stock-gains-1-77).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: WIT is +7.19% over 5 sessions, which is what a sector re-rating on peer beats looks like. What is not fully in the price is Wipro-specific BFSI recovery; previews still have Wipro as the only large-cap declining in cc, so a flat-ish print would read as better than the -1% end of the poll.
findings.independence: HCLTech Q2 FY27 (https://www.freepressjournal.in/business/hcltech-net-profit-rises-21-to-5132-crore-in-q2-fy27-revenue-up-115, 2026-10-12) and Accenture Q4 FY26 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001467373/000146737326000037/q4fy26earnings8-kexhibit.htm) are separate documents pointing the same way; all three are peer proxies, not Wipro numbers.

findings.finding: Some Wipro large-deal closures and ramp-ups slipped from Q1 into Q2 per management on the Q1 call (MOFSL note, 2026-07-16), so Q2 bookings / large-deal TCV and the ramp feeding the Q3 guide have a documented tailwind; PL expects Q2 deal wins of $2.7-2.8bn against Q1's $3.37bn total and $1.63bn large-deal TCV.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 (Oct 2025): large-deal wins were the standout positive yet Indian shares fell up to 4.6% on the guide (https://ticker.finology.in/discover/market-update/wipro-q2-fy26-results-analysis-deal-wins); bookings have not outweighed a soft guide on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The slippage remark sits in a broker note body, not the wire; the PL $2.7-2.8bn bookings bar is below Q1, so a slipped-deal catch-up would print bookings above the bar. If priced, previews would model bookings above Q1, which they do not.
findings.independence: Q1 release large-deal TCV $1,626m +12.9% q/q cc (https://www.itiger.com/hans/news/2651420824) shows momentum in the same direction; same company, different document.

findings.finding: Wipro's Q3 guide is the line, consensus expects -2% to 0% cc for the furlough-seasonal December quarter, and Wipro has sold off on its forward guide on three of its last four prints (Q2 FY26 India -4.6%, Q3 FY26 India -9.5% / ADR >-3% post-market, Q4 FY26 India ~-4% / ADR -2.2%), with Q1 FY27 the exception (ADR -0.28%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As stated: guide-driven sell-offs Oct 2025, Jan 2026, Apr 2026; flat ADR in Jul 2026 on a -1.5% to +0.5% guide (https://www.theweek.in/wire-updates/business/2026/01/19/wipro-shares-tumble-nearly-10-pc-post-q3-numbers.html; https://www.businesstoday.in/amp/markets/stocks/story/wipro-adr-slips-over-2-after-q4-fy26-results-whats-driving-the-move-526034-2026-04-16).
findings.why_not_priced: The bar is public; what is not in the price after a 7% sector run-up is this name's reaction habit on the guide line. If the market had priced a soft Q3 guide, WIT would have lagged the peer rally rather than gaining 7% in five sessions.
findings.independence: MOFSL Q1 note models FY27 flat to slightly negative and Wipro lagging peers (same broker as finding 2, different claim). Reaction history from separate news reports per quarter.

findings.finding: WIT ran +7.19% over 5 sessions into the print on peer read-through (ACN, TCS), raising the bar for a company whose own guide still implies a cc decline; the move is sector beta rather than Wipro-specific news.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26: domestic shares rallied into the print and fell ~9.5% after (https://ticker.finology.in/discover/market-update/wipro-q3-fy26-quarterly-results-analysis).
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is itself the price; the claim is that it embeds a peer-level outcome Wipro's own guide does not support. Baseline run_up_5d_pct +7.19 is the evidence.
findings.independence: Shares the TCS document with finding 1 (opposite reading: finding 1 is the fundamental read-through, this one is the bar it raises). Baseline tape is the independent datum.

findings.finding: ADR short interest rose ~63% from 62.96m (2026-08-14) to 103.6m (2026-09-15) and held at 102.75m on 2026-09-30, 14.18 days to cover on falling ADR volume: an in-line or better Q3 guide meets a crowded ADR short.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No sourced ADR squeeze on a prior Wipro print; ADR moves have been smaller than Indian-share moves on the last prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is on FINRA with a lag and not in any preview; the 14 DTC is relative to ADR turnover only, and the ADR can be arbitraged against the Indian line, which caps a squeeze.
findings.independence: Baseline put/call OI 3.42 (thin, 615 contracts) is consistent with bearish ADR positioning; none from a separate source.

findings.finding: Wipro's 2026-09-30 filing pushed completion of the Alpha Net Consulting contract acquisition (up to $70.8m consideration) from 30 Sept to 31 Dec 2026, so it contributes nothing to Q2, while Emkay's -1% USD Q2 estimate explicitly includes Mindsprint and AlphaNet.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history; acquisition contributions are small relative to $2.6bn quarterly revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: At least one broker estimate still carries AlphaNet in Q2; unclear whether the company guide did. Contribution likely well under 0.5% of revenue, so small either way.
findings.independence: Emkay's inclusion of AlphaNet is in https://www.kotakneo.com/news/stocks/wipro-q2-fy27-results-preview/ (2026-10-14); the June delay is in https://upstox.com/news/market-news/stocks/wipro-revises-timeline-for-alpha-net-contract-acquisition-targets-september-end-completion/article-195862/.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-08 the US Labor Department suspended Wipro (with TCS, Infosys, HCL, Cognizant and others) from the PERM green-card programme; Wipro's call (2026-10-15, 9:30 ET) is the first Wipro management comment on it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: TCS (2026-10-09) and HCL (2026-10-12) reported after the suspension and their stocks rose; Infosys said no material impact.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: sector-wide, public, and peers rallied through it. Residual is a question on the call about US delivery cost.
findings.independence: https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/global-daily-news/infosys-sees-little-impact-from-perm-program-ban (Infosys says little impact), which argues the size toward zero.

outside_window.finding: Infosys reports Q2 FY27 on 2026-10-23, after the exit window; its guide read-through cannot reach this trade.

baseline_tension: No option skew to agree or disagree with; the +7% 5-day run-up on peer beats cuts against the guide-sell-off pattern, and the crowded ADR short cuts against any negative, so the evidence nets to roughly zero.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sells its prints): peer read-through finding on the reported quarter cut +0.5 -> +0.3.
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): guide-sell-off finding cut -0.7 -> -0.5 and run-up finding -0.5 -> -0.3 given 14.2 days to cover on the ADR; p_up moved 46 -> 47.
